intended_object: The punctured closed star of a vertex v in the geometric realization |K| of an abstract simplicial complex: the closed star |St(v)| (union of closed simplices of faces containing v) with the apex point v removed. Inferred from the docstring, the module doc (Rourke–Sanderson cone/link), and the lemma puncturedClosedStar_eq_sdiff_vertex.
explanation: closedStarRealization K {v} is the set of points whose carrier τ satisfies τ ∪ {v} ∈ K, i.e. points lying in a closed simplex of a face containing v; this is the geometric closed star. The extra condition x(v) < 1 removes exactly the vertex v: realization points have nonnegative coordinates summing to 1, so x(v) = 1 forces x to be the vertex. The library proves this as puncturedClosedStar_eq_sdiff_vertex (the set equals closedStarRealization K {v} \ {vertex K v}). Degenerate case: for an isolated vertex the closed star is {v}, so the punctured star is empty, which is correct. The vertex type is arbitrary, with only DecidableEq needed to form {v}, so the definition is not too narrow. Mathlib has no geometric realization of abstract simplicial complexes or star constructions on one, so there is no counterpart.
